restrictions: Messages are exactly 135 bytes; each is one padded block M || 0x86 with zero capacity (520 fixed state bits). Complete fixed-zero-IV SHA3-256 sponge with suffix 0x06 and pad10*1, prefix rounds 0..4, 256-bit digest.

No advice: the algorithm runs every phase itself - the trail search P (trail_search in the experiment file, whose T3 counter of full evaluations raises CapReached above F_CAP = 2^22), the advice program B', setup S, the connector and the enumeration E - and the claimed time is the sum of caps and exact counts times counted prices (proof 2, 6), unchanged from v10: P 2^32.71 units (T1 8,674,833 nodes x 2^12; T2 1,639,088,128 leaves x 166; T3 5,679,328,446 batches x 1,583; full evaluations at F_CAP x 2^13; 1411 group setups x 2^27); B' 2^32 units plus one update, at most 2^26 units per candidate; at most 2^13 connector attempts of at most 2^18 work units; E: K = 96 spaces of 2^24 batches of 256 pairs at 6,112 primitives per batch on every path; at most 2^11 stage-2 pairs per space. Total 2^34.1359, claimed 34.14. No expected value is charged.

P outputs the trail of proof 3 within F_CAP: a deterministic premise from two native runs over all 1.4 x 10^12 leaves (F = 770 in the algorithm's order; 1,896,302 in pass 1, which bounds the algorithm's F for any core order by proof Lemma P, 2.2 times below F_CAP; Appendix A). The organizer executes the algorithm's own P on sub-problems (r5-count trials 24-27): it reproduces the native per-core output and F (517, 0, 425) and stops at a lowered cap. E is v8's E as a function of the space (proof Lemma 4).

Development runs are not charged and are disclosed (proof 0, unchanged): they fixed B''s six design constants (75 processes, 1,559 CPU-s) and the connector's DMIN = 33 and 2^18 cap. The success bound uses only runs made after: pre-registrations C (48 runs) and D (their completion). Sensitivity, not claimed: B''s development at 2^38 primitives per core-second gives 38.29, v7's whole ledger 41.22.

Probability space: the algorithm's own coins (B' candidate coins, connector coins), fixed target, no advice. Success is measured end to end (proof 5): each of the 48 runs of pre-registration C, completed by pre-registration D, is a complete run of the algorithm (Lemma 6), and 46 of 48 output a collision. The one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound is 0.874 (0.877 with the extra smoke-test run, 47 of 49). Claimed 0.40, which the data would still support with as few as 26 successes in 48. No per-advice, per-candidate or dispersion premise is used.

Executed evidence (not the claimed cost): pre-registration C (plan, driver, analysis and enumerator hashed at 2026-10-07T16:55:25Z before any run; 48 fresh runs, all reported; B', the connector rule and E on the first 16 spaces) and pre-registration D (plan hashed at 17:53:16Z before any run; E on the remaining spaces of the 30 runs without an output, in order, up to the first output; plus the smoke-test run 999). Neither plan has a submit or withhold rule. Every other run made during v11, including a parallel session's abandoned variant runs, is listed in proof 4.1 and enters no bound; so do pre-registration A, pre-registration B and the v6 run. r5-C-0..4 replay a positive space of C and a success of D from their labels and return real collisions; r5-bp-0..4 and r5-bpfull re-derive A and run B' whole with both caps acting; 15 of C's collisions are certificates.

Th0rgal is a co-author: 7deb1595 (with Subflatus3 and rubenmarcus) gave the zero-advice framing used here (v8's E also used its early-abort row order; v10's bitsliced E evaluates all equations). Memory: largest phase about 224 MB (T3's triple tables in the counted program); declared 30.

The nominal reference identifier does not assert an improvement over published work; no improvement on the method of Guo et al. is claimed beyond the byte-aligned adaptation, B', the bitsliced counted E and T3 and the accounting.

heuristics.statement: Averaged over all of the algorithm's own coins (B' candidate coins, connector coins), the probability p that the algorithm outputs a collision satisfies p >= p0 = 0.874. Premise R (run selection and coins): the SHA-256/SHAKE-256 coins of labels fixed before the runs act as fresh coins, and the 48 runs of pre-registration C, completed by pre-registration D, are an unselected sample of the algorithm's runs.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability. Each run of C completed by D is a complete run of the algorithm with label-derived coins (proof Lemma 6: B''s budget and the connector's A_ADV and A_MAX never acted, E ran on the 96 accepted spaces in order, and the stage-2 cap never bound), so its success indicator is the algorithm's. The claim 0.40 needs p >= 0.40; output correctness and every cost cap hold without H1.
heuristics.extrapolation: 46 of the 48 runs of C succeed: 18 had an output among their first 16 spaces (C), and D found an output for 28 of the other 30, at spaces 19-77; runs 22 and 26 had none in 96. The runs use distinct labels, so their outcomes are independent, and p0 is the one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound (exact binomial tail). With the smoke-test run 999 (made after C's plan, outside its sample; output at space 23), 47 of 49 succeed and the bound is 0.877. 0.40 would still be the 95% bound with 26 successes in 48. Premise R: both plans, their drivers, analyses and enumerator were hashed before any run (C at 16:55:25Z, D at 17:53:16Z); every run is reported in a per-run table (proof 4.3); no rule to submit or withhold depends on the outcome; every other run made during v11 is listed (proof 4.1); the production seed is the organizer's public seed and only picks which logged successes are replayed. Organizer checks: r5-C-0..4 re-derive sampled successes of C and D from their labels (B', connector attempts, E) and return the collisions; r5-bp-0..4 and r5-bpfull execute the B' and connector programs. Descriptive consistency: 0.0299 positive spaces per space in C against 0.0265 predicted by the trail; constant s would give 0.946 per run, and 0.958 was observed.
heuristics.limitations: 48 complete runs. Label-seeded SHAKE-256 coins stand in for fresh words (premise R). The runs' E is fes.c (exact enumeration, checked against logged runs and by self-checks at 64 points per space; Lemma 4 makes it the same function of the space as the counted E). Failures and the order of spaces are reported by us; the organizer re-derives sampled successes only. P's output is the deterministic premise of proof 2.1.
